reporting_conventions.cost_saving: Positive saving_fraction means lower candidate cost than reference. README percentage displays multiply the saved fraction by 100, then round; no performance statistic is recomputed.
reporting_conventions.patient_difference: extra_patient_losses is candidate minus reference, in simulated losses per complete 52-step world; negative is favorable.
reporting_conventions.cost_unit: Original simulated cost units, not observed clinical expenditures.
reporting_conventions.harm_counts: Numbers of paired worlds marked cost- or patient-harmed by the existing comparison; not independent patient observations.
reporting_conventions.intervals: Saved descriptive 95% intervals, unadjusted for multiplicity. Distinct source interval types are retained, not selected by significance.
reporting_conventions.missing_values: A field absent from the existing source remains absent; absence does not mean zero or a completed test.
reporting_conventions.integer_identity_preservation: Unsafe IEEE-754 integer seed identities are copied as exact JSON number literals using JSON.rawJSON; not rounded or reseeded.

interpretation_record: Existing comparison only; no new scientific computation or re-analysis.
Graph proposal costs 0.324533 percent less than Local, with paired-world descriptive interval spanning zero. This is not a three-percent result or equal-information architecture attribution.
Graph proposal costs 0.122923 percent less than the global proposal and 0.072964 percent less than the zero-update proposal plus H8; both paired-world intervals span zero.
Graph proposal costs 2.935222 percent more than retained old Graph and has 17.25 additional simulated patient losses per world. This pilot does not support replacing old Graph.

Old Graph costs 1.053013 percent less than unchanged old Self on this new panel; mean patient losses fall by 22.333333, but its paired-world patient interval spans zero and nine worlds have increased patient loss.
Graph proposal is selected on average 1.416667 of 52 decisions. Sparse proposal use is a possible bottleneck, not an established causal diagnosis.
New versus old changes learning algorithm, training worlds (24 versus 96), and candidate cap (15 versus 14), so this is not an isolated PPO or GCN superiority test.
DEVELOPMENT, synthetic-only, three blocks; all pair, condition, block and world harms remain in the original comparison.

limitations: Both panels are DEVELOPMENT and synthetic-only. The old models supply three trained blocks, not 72, 24 or six independent training replications.
No pooling or new independent-training uncertainty calculation was performed.
The 72-world Graph/Self joint descriptive screen passed, but harmed worlds and heterogeneous block effects remain.
Graph/H8 failed its joint patient screen because condition 2 had additional mean patient losses despite overall cost and patient averages improving.
Graph/Flat did not establish an architecture advantage; retain the interval crossing zero and mean patient increase.
The 24-world old Graph/Self patient paired-world interval spans zero and condition 1 has positive mean additional losses.
New PPO and old controls differ in algorithm, training worlds per model and candidate cap; the pilot is not isolated proof of PPO inferiority or superior GCN representation.
The fixed PPO promotion rule and its three-percent flag did not pass.
No clinical safety, corrected significance, universal architecture superiority, deployment or publication guarantee.
